proposals.before: Later he charged a white hare, was thrown and hurt, and told the omen.
proposals.after: Later he saw a white hare, galloped to shoot it; his horse fell and he was injured, then he told what he had seen.
proposals.sourceQuote: 後見白兔，馳射之，馬倒被傷，乃說所見。
proposals.sourceReason: 後見白兔馳射之 is see then gallop-and-shoot, not merely charge; 乃說所見 narrates what was seen, not an omen gloss.

proposals.before: He died in Yonghe 4 (348 CE) after fifteen years on the throne, aged fifty-two.
proposals.after: He died in the fourth year of Yonghe after fifteen years on the throne, aged fifty-two.
proposals.sourceQuote: 以永和四年死，在位十五年，時年五十二。
proposals.sourceReason: Chinese gives only 永和四年 with tenure and age; the western year 348 CE is not in the source sentence.

proposals.before: Murong Han (defector general).
proposals.after: Murong Han.
proposals.sourceQuote: 慕容翰
proposals.sourceReason: Unit is the bare personal-name heading 慕容翰; parenthetical defector general is editorial addition.

proposals.before: He was bold, cunning, a superb archer, and immensely strong.
proposals.after: He was heroic and bold, full of stratagems, ape-armed and skilled at archery, with strength that surpassed others.
proposals.sourceQuote: 性雄豪，多權略，猿臂工射，膂力過人。
proposals.sourceReason: 性雄豪多權略 needs heroic boldness and abundant stratagem, not cunning; 猿臂工射 must keep the ape-arms detail.

proposals.before: Duan Liao honored him after his defection.
proposals.after: When he fled to Duan Liao, he was deeply respected and loved by Liao.
proposals.sourceQuote: 及奔段遼，深為遼所敬愛。
proposals.sourceReason: 及奔段遼 states flight to Liao; 深為遼所敬愛 is deep respect and love, not merely honored after defection.

proposals.before: After the defeat at Liucheng, Duan Lan wanted to push on, but Murong Han feigned advice that spared Yan a deeper strike.
proposals.after: After the defeat at Liucheng, Duan Lan wanted to ride the victory and push deep; Murong Han, fearing this would bring harm on his native state, gave Lan deceitful counsel, and Lan then did not advance.
proposals.sourceQuote: 柳城之敗，段蘭欲乘勝深入，翰慮成本國之害，詭說于蘭，蘭遂不進。
proposals.sourceReason: Must keep 乘勝深入, 慮成本國之害, 詭說于蘭, and 蘭遂不進 as distinct propositions.

proposals.before: Murong Huang’s host is elite.
proposals.after: The King of Yan has come in person; his soldiers and horses are elite.
proposals.sourceQuote: 燕王自來，士馬精銳。
proposals.sourceReason: 燕王自來 is personal arrival of the Yan king; 士馬精銳 is elite troops and mounts, not host alone.

proposals.before: War is peril—if you lose here, how will you hold the south?”
proposals.after: Weapons are ill-omened tools, and battle holds peril; if you lose here, how will you defend the south?”
proposals.sourceQuote: 兵者凶器，戰有危慮，若其失利，何以南禦乎！」
proposals.sourceReason: 兵者凶器 is the opening idiom and must be kept; 戰有危慮 and 何以南禦 close the warning.

proposals.before: He chased Huang and was crushed.
proposals.after: He then led his forces to pursue Huang, and Lan was indeed crushingly defeated.
proposals.sourceQuote: 乃率眾追皝，蘭果大敗。
proposals.sourceReason: 乃率眾追皝 states leading the host in pursuit; 蘭果大敗 marks the indeed-fulfilled great defeat.

proposals.before: Even in exile Murong Han worked secretly for Yan’s good.
proposals.after: Although Murong Han dwelt in an enemy state, he established loyalty through the course of events—all cases were of this kind.
proposals.sourceQuote: 翰雖處仇國，因事立忠，皆此類也。
proposals.sourceReason: 因事立忠 is loyalty shown amid events, not secret work for Yan; 皆此類也 must remain as the summary.

proposals.before: Yuwen Gui sent a hundred picked riders after him.
proposals.after: Han then fled, and Gui sent over a hundred picked cavalry to pursue him.
proposals.sourceQuote: 既而逃，歸乃遣勁騎百餘追之。
proposals.sourceReason: 既而逃 is Han’s flight before 歸乃遣勁騎百餘追之; both steps are required.

proposals.before: You know my archery—do not force a fight.
proposals.after: You know my bow and arrows well enough—do not press me and bring death on yourselves.
proposals.sourceQuote: 吾之弓矢，汝曹足知，無為相逼，自取死也。
proposals.sourceReason: 無為相逼自取死也 warns against pressing him and thereby seeking their own deaths; archery fame alone is incomplete.

proposals.before: My bow and arrows, you lot fully know; do not force each other, self-seeking death.
proposals.after: My bow and arrows you lot fully know; do not press me and seek your own deaths.
proposals.sourceQuote: 吾之弓矢，汝曹足知，無為相逼，自取死也。
proposals.sourceReason: 相逼 is pressing the speaker, not forcing each other; 自取死也 is bringing death on yourselves.

proposals.before: Plant a blade at a hundred paces—if I ring it, withdraw;
proposals.after: Plant a blade at a hundred paces—if I hit it, withdraw;
proposals.sourceQuote: 汝可百步豎刀，吾射中者，汝便宜反；
proposals.sourceReason: 吾射中者 means if the shot hits; 刀鐶 appears only in the next unit and should not be imported here.

proposals.before: When he tried riding at home, informers called it sedition.
proposals.after: Later, as his illness gradually improved, he tried riding at home to test himself; someone reported that Han was privately practising riding and suspected something extraordinary.
proposals.sourceQuote: 後疾漸愈，於其家中騎馬自試，或有人告翰私習騎，疑為非常。
proposals.sourceReason: 後疾漸愈 and 騎馬自試 precede the denunciation; 私習騎 and 疑為非常 are report and suspicion, not a bare sedition gloss.

proposals.before: Huang, who had always feared him, sent him poison.
proposals.after: Huang, who had long been jealous of him, thereupon granted him death.
proposals.sourceQuote: 皝素忌之，遂賜死焉。
proposals.sourceReason: 素忌之 is long jealousy or wariness; 賜死 is granting death, while poison is only stated later in 仰藥而死.

proposals.before: Huang plain envied him; thereupon granted death.
proposals.after: Huang had long been jealous of him; thereupon granted him death.
proposals.sourceQuote: 皝素忌之，遂賜死焉。
proposals.sourceReason: 素忌之 needs long-standing jealousy or wariness; plain envied is unclear wording for the same fact.

proposals.before: Murong Han told the messenger, “I fled in fear and deserved death, yet I would not die in a foreign hall, so I came home to face judgment.
proposals.after: Nearing death Murong Han told the envoy, “Han harbored distrust and fled abroad; my crime is too great for death to atone; I could not leave my bones in a rebel court, so I returned to submit to the authorities.
proposals.sourceQuote: 翰臨死謂使者曰：「翰懷疑外奔，罪不容誅，不能以骸骨委賊庭，故歸罪有司。
proposals.sourceReason: 罪不容誅 marks guilt beyond mere execution; 歸罪有司 is submitting to officials, after refusing 賊庭 bones.

proposals.before: Han nearing death told the envoy: “Han harbored suspicion and fled abroad; crime does not permit execution; could not cast bones in the bandit court; therefore returned guilt to the responsible officials.
proposals.after: Han nearing death told the envoy: “Han harbored suspicion and fled abroad; the crime is too great for death to atone; I could not cast my bones in the bandit court; therefore I returned to submit to the responsible officials.
proposals.sourceQuote: 翰臨死謂使者曰：「翰懷疑外奔，罪不容誅，不能以骸骨委賊庭，故歸罪有司。
proposals.sourceReason: 歸罪有司 means submitting oneself to the authorities for punishment, not returning guilt onto them.

proposals.before: Under Wang Jun he rose to administration aide but was distrusted.
proposals.after: When Wang Jun held the province, Yu was transferred to administration aide; Jun was jealous and would not employ him.
proposals.sourceQuote: 王浚領州，轉治中從事，忌而不能任。
proposals.sourceReason: 轉治中從事 is the transfer; 忌而不能任 is jealousy plus refusal or failure to employ, not distrust alone.

proposals.before: Shi Le asked, "If what you say is so, why did Duke Wang not employ him?"
proposals.after: Shi Le asked, "If what you say is so, why did Duke Wang not employ them?"
proposals.sourceQuote: 勒曰：「若如君言，王公何以不任？」
proposals.sourceReason: Song has just named Liu Han and Yang Yu; 何以不任 refers to not employing them, not only him.

proposals.before: Cheng Pan replied, “China is shattered; beyond the Yi River there is no refuge.
proposals.after: Cheng Pan replied, “Now Huaxia is split and crumbling, the nine provinces torn apart; where proper tracks reach is only as far as the Yi River.
proposals.sourceQuote: 泮曰：「今華夏分崩，九州幅裂，軌跡所及，易水而已。
proposals.sourceReason: 軌跡所及易水而已 means civil order’s reach ends at the Yi, not that there is no refuge beyond it.

proposals.before: Desiring to recline and await the great penetration—waiting for the Yellow River to clear—is waiting for the river to clear.
proposals.after: To wish to live in proud reclusion (as in the “Kao pan”) and wait for a great opening is to wait for the Yellow River to run clear.
proposals.sourceQuote: 欲偃蹇考槃，以待大通者，俟河之清也。
proposals.sourceReason: 偃蹇考槃以待大通 is reclusive waiting for a great thaw; 俟河之清也 is the single impossibility simile, not a doubled clause.

proposals.before: Let both sides forget old quarrels and restore peace so the realm stands firm as Taishan and the people can lay down their burdens.”
proposals.after: Let both sides remedy their former faults and renew good faith as at the beginning, so the state may have the security of Mount Tai and the common people receive the blessing of laying down their burdens.”
proposals.sourceQuote: 願兩追前失，通款如初，使國家有太山之安，蒼生蒙息肩之惠。」
proposals.sourceReason: 兩追前失 is remedy former faults, not forget quarrels; 通款如初 and 太山/息肩 images must stay.

proposals.before: Murong Huang, who had long admired him, freed him at once, named him palace director, then promoted him to senior major on his staff.
proposals.after: Murong Huang, who had long heard of Yu’s name, at once ordered his bonds released, appointed him Palace Director, then promoted him to Grand General’s Left Major.
proposals.sourceQuote: 皝素聞裕名，即命釋其囚，拜郎中令，遷大將軍左司馬。
proposals.sourceReason: 素聞裕名 is long hearing of the name; offices are 郎中令 then 大將軍左司馬, not a vague senior major.

proposals.before: Huang plain had heard Yu’s name; immediately ordered release his bonds; appointed Palace Director; promoted Grand General’s Left Major.
proposals.after: Huang had long heard of Yu’s name; immediately ordered his bonds released; appointed Palace Director; promoted him to Grand General’s Left Major.
proposals.sourceQuote: 皝素聞裕名，即命釋其囚，拜郎中令，遷大將軍左司馬。
proposals.sourceReason: 素聞 needs had long heard; plain had heard is unclear, while the two office steps remain exact.

proposals.before: Though he rose above older favorites, he lived modestly and treated everyone like a poor scholar.
proposals.after: Although Yang Yu served Huang and grew daily closer, with favor and rank above the old retainers, his nature was humble, respectful, pure and frugal, firm, simple, kind and earnest; though he repeatedly held posts at the apex of the court, he was like a scholar in plain cloth.
proposals.sourceQuote: 裕雖仕皝日近，寵秩在舊人之右，性謙恭清儉，剛簡慈篤，雖曆居朝端，若布衣之士。
proposals.sourceReason: Must keep 仕皝日近、寵秩在舊人之右, the virtue string 謙恭清儉剛簡慈篤, and 朝端若布衣之士.

proposals.before: Lu Chen of Fanyang once said, “In times of peace I have known many officials, but few match Yang Yu in loyalty, austerity, and steadfast faith.”
proposals.after: Earlier, Lu Chen of Fanyang always praised him, saying, “I have lived through Jin’s clear peace and have broadly observed many court gentlemen; loyal, pure, concise and resolute, steadfast in faith and fierce in righteousness—men like Yang Shilun are in truth few.”
proposals.sourceQuote: 初，范陽盧諶每稱之曰：「吾及晉之清平，曆觀朝士多矣，忠清簡毅，篤信義烈，如陽士倫者，實亦未幾。」
proposals.sourceReason: Quote needs 晉之清平, the full 忠清簡毅篤信義烈 string, and courtesy name 陽士倫, not a thinned paraphrase.

proposals.before: minister of the Duan
proposals.after: served the Duan house
proposals.sourceQuote: 曆事段氏五主，甚見尊重。
proposals.sourceReason: 曆事段氏 means successively served the Duan house’s lords, not holding a post titled minister of the Duan.

sourceUnits.zh: 慕容皝
sourceUnits.en: Murong Huang.
sourceUnits.literal: Murong Huang.

sourceUnits.zh: 皝親臨東庠考試學生，其經通秀異者，擢充近侍。
sourceUnits.en: He tested students at the eastern school and promoted the best as attendants.
sourceUnits.literal: Huang personally arrived at the eastern school to examine students; those whose classics were thorough and outstanding, promoted to fill close attendance.

sourceUnits.zh: 以久旱，丐百姓田租。
sourceUnits.en: He remitted rent during a drought.
sourceUnits.literal: Because of long drought, begged off common people’s field rent.

sourceUnits.zh: 罷成周、冀陽、營丘等郡。
sourceUnits.en: He abolished several empty commanderies such as Chengzhou, Jiyang, and Yingqiu.
sourceUnits.literal: Abolished Chengzhou, Jiyang, Yingqiu, and other commanderies.

sourceUnits.zh: 以勃海人為興集縣，河間人為寧集縣，廣平、魏郡人為興平縣，東萊、北海人為育黎縣，吳人為吳縣，悉隸燕國。
sourceUnits.en: He grouped refugees from Bohai, Hejian, Guangping, Wei, Donglai, Beihai, and Wu into new counties under Yan.
sourceUnits.literal: Made Bohai people Xingji county, Hejian people Ningji county, Guangping and Wei commandery people Xingping county, Donglai and Beihai people Yuli county, Wu people Wu county—all subordinate to the state of Yan.

sourceUnits.zh: 皝嘗畋於西鄙，將濟河，見一父老，服硃衣，乘白馬，舉手麾皝曰：「此非獵所，王其還也。」
sourceUnits.en: While hunting on the western frontier Murong Huang was about to cross a river when he saw an old man in cinnabar robes on a white horse, who waved him off and said, "This is not a place for hunting; Your Majesty should return."
sourceUnits.literal: Huang once hunted on the western border, about to cross the River, saw an old man, dressed cinnabar robes, riding a white horse, raised hand and waved Huang, saying: “This is not a hunting place; the king ought to return.”

sourceUnits.zh: 秘之不言，遂濟河，連日大獲。
sourceUnits.en: He kept silent, crossed the river, and enjoyed great sport for days.
sourceUnits.literal: He concealed it and did not speak, thereupon crossed the River, continuously days great catch.

sourceUnits.zh: 後見白兔，馳射之，馬倒被傷，乃說所見。
sourceUnits.en: Later he charged a white hare, was thrown and hurt, and told the omen.
sourceUnits.literal: Later saw white hare, galloped and shot it; horse fell and he was injured, then narrated what he had seen.

sourceUnits.zh: 輦而還宮，引俊屬以後事。
sourceUnits.en: They carried him home; he briefed Murong Jun on the succession.
sourceUnits.literal: Carried on litter returned palace, led Jun to entrust later affairs.

sourceUnits.zh: 以永和四年死，在位十五年，時年五十二。
sourceUnits.en: He died in Yonghe 4 (348 CE) after fifteen years on the throne, aged fifty-two.
sourceUnits.literal: Died in the fourth year of Yonghe, fifteen years on the throne, age fifty-two sui.

sourceUnits.zh: 俊僭號，追諡文明皇帝。
sourceUnits.en: After Murong Jun took the throne he posthumously styled his father Emperor Wenming.
sourceUnits.literal: When Jun illegitimately assumed imperial title, posthumously honored him as Emperor Wenming.

sourceUnits.zh: 慕容翰
sourceUnits.en: Murong Han (defector general).
sourceUnits.literal: Murong Han.

sourceUnits.zh: 慕容翰，字元邕，廆之庶長子也。
sourceUnits.en: Murong Han, courtesy name Yuanyong, was Murong Hui’s eldest son by a concubine.
sourceUnits.literal: Murong Han, courtesy name Yuanyong, was Hui’s eldest son by a concubine.

sourceUnits.zh: 性雄豪，多權略，猿臂工射，膂力過人。
sourceUnits.en: He was bold, cunning, a superb archer, and immensely strong.
sourceUnits.literal: Nature heroic and bold, abundant in stratagem; ape arms skilled at shooting; physical strength surpassed others.

sourceUnits.zh: 廆甚奇之，委以折沖之任。
sourceUnits.en: Murong Hui prized him and gave him the hardest fighting assignments.
sourceUnits.literal: Hui greatly wondered at him, entrusted him with the charge of breaking the enemy’s momentum.

sourceUnits.zh: 行師征伐，所在有功，威聲大振，為遠近所憚。
sourceUnits.en: Every campaign brought success; neighbors far and near feared him.
sourceUnits.literal: When lines marched and campaigned, wherever he went had merit; awe-inspiring name greatly shook, feared by far and near.

sourceUnits.zh: 作鎮遼東，高句麗不敢為寇。
sourceUnits.en: While he held Liaodong, Goguryeo dared not raid.
sourceUnits.literal: As garrison commander in Liaodong, Goguryeo did not dare make raids.

sourceUnits.zh: 善撫接，愛儒學，自士大夫至於卒伍，莫不樂而從之。
sourceUnits.en: He won men from gentry to ranks by kindness and a love of learning.
sourceUnits.literal: Skilled at comforting and drawing near, loved classical learning; from grandees down to common soldiers, none did not joyfully follow him.

sourceUnits.zh: 及奔段遼，深為遼所敬愛。
sourceUnits.en: Duan Liao honored him after his defection.
sourceUnits.literal: When he fled to Duan Liao, deeply was respected and loved by Liao.

sourceUnits.zh: 柳城之敗，段蘭欲乘勝深入，翰慮成本國之害，詭說于蘭，蘭遂不進。
sourceUnits.en: After the defeat at Liucheng, Duan Lan wanted to push on, but Murong Han feigned advice that spared Yan a deeper strike.
sourceUnits.literal: At Liucheng’s defeat, Duan Lan wished to ride victory to penetrate deep; Han worried it would complete harm to his native state, deceitfully spoke to Lan; Lan then did not advance.

sourceUnits.zh: 後石季龍征遼，皝親將三軍略令支以北，遼議欲追之，翰知皝躬自總戎，戰必克勝，乃謂遼曰：「今石氏向至，方對大故，不宜復以小小為事。
sourceUnits.en: Later when Shi Hu campaigned against Duan Liao and Murong Huang personally led an army to raid north of Lingzhi, Duan Liao debated pursuit. Knowing Huang commanded in person and must win, Murong Han told Duan Liao, "Now the Shi are about to arrive and you face a great enemy; you should not again take up small matters.
sourceUnits.literal: Later Shi Jilong campaigned against Liao; Huang personally led the three armies raiding north of Lingzhi; Liao debated wishing to pursue him; Han knew Huang personally commanded the army, battle must seize victory; thereupon said to Liao: “Now the Shi clan is about to arrive, just facing great enemy; ought not again to take small matters as affairs.

sourceUnits.zh: 燕王自來，士馬精銳。
sourceUnits.en: Murong Huang’s host is elite.
sourceUnits.literal: The King of Yan has come in person; soldiers and horses are picked and sharp.

sourceUnits.zh: 兵者凶器，戰有危慮，若其失利，何以南禦乎！」
sourceUnits.en: War is peril—if you lose here, how will you hold the south?”
sourceUnits.literal: Weapons are ill-omened tools; battle has perilous anxiety; if it misses advantage, how to defend the south!”

sourceUnits.zh: 蘭怒曰：「吾前聽卿誑說，致成今患，不復入卿計中矣。」
sourceUnits.en: Duan Lan snapped, “Your last ‘advice’ ruined me—I will not heed you again.”
sourceUnits.literal: Lan angrily said: “Formerly I listened to your deceitful talk, caused to complete today’s disaster; I do not again enter your schemes.”

sourceUnits.zh: 乃率眾追皝，蘭果大敗。
sourceUnits.en: He chased Huang and was crushed.
sourceUnits.literal: Thereupon led host to pursue Huang; Lan was indeed greatly defeated.

sourceUnits.zh: 翰雖處仇國，因事立忠，皆此類也。
sourceUnits.en: Even in exile Murong Han worked secretly for Yan’s good.
sourceUnits.literal: Although Han dwelt in an enemy state, by events established loyalty—all was of this kind.

sourceUnits.zh: 及遼奔走，翰又北投宇文歸。
sourceUnits.en: When Duan Liao fled in defeat, Han again went north to Yuwen Gui.
sourceUnits.literal: When Liao fled in defeat, Han again north threw himself to Yuwen Gui.

sourceUnits.zh: 既而逃，歸乃遣勁騎百餘追之。
sourceUnits.en: Yuwen Gui sent a hundred picked riders after him.
sourceUnits.literal: Having then fled, Gui thereupon sent fierce cavalry over a hundred to pursue him.

sourceUnits.zh: 翰遙謂追者曰：「吾既思戀而歸，理無反面。
sourceUnits.en: He shouted to them, “I mean to go home—I will not turn back.
sourceUnits.literal: Han from afar told the pursuers: “I already long to return; in principle there is no turning back.

sourceUnits.zh: 吾之弓矢，汝曹足知，無為相逼，自取死也。
sourceUnits.en: You know my archery—do not force a fight.
sourceUnits.literal: My bow and arrows, you lot fully know; do not force each other, self-seeking death.

sourceUnits.zh: 吾處汝國久，恨不殺汝。
sourceUnits.en: I have lived among you too long—I should have killed you.
sourceUnits.literal: I have dwelt in your state long; I regret not killing you.

sourceUnits.zh: 汝可百步豎刀，吾射中者，汝便宜反；
sourceUnits.en: Plant a blade at a hundred paces—if I ring it, withdraw;
sourceUnits.literal: You can at a hundred paces set up a blade; if I shoot the center, you then conveniently turn back;

sourceUnits.zh: 不中者，可來前也。」
sourceUnits.en: if I miss, come on.”
sourceUnits.literal: if not center, you may come forward.”

sourceUnits.zh: 歸騎解刀豎之，翰一發便中刀鐶，追騎乃散。
sourceUnits.en: They fixed a blade; his first arrow struck the ring and they broke off the chase.
sourceUnits.literal: Gui’s riders undid a blade and set it up; Han one shot then hit the blade ring; pursuing riders then scattered.

sourceUnits.zh: 既至，皝甚加恩禮，
sourceUnits.en: Huang welcomed him with rich honors.
sourceUnits.literal: Having arrived, Huang greatly added favor and ceremony.

sourceUnits.zh: 建元二年，從皝討宇文歸，臨陣為流矢所中，臥病積時。
sourceUnits.en: In the second year of Jianyuan, he joined the war on Yuwen Gui, took a stray shaft, and lay long ill.
sourceUnits.literal: In the second year of Jianyuan, he followed Huang to campaign against Yuwen Gui; on the line of battle he was struck by a stray arrow; he lay ill a long time.

sourceUnits.zh: 後疾漸愈，於其家中騎馬自試，或有人告翰私習騎，疑為非常。
sourceUnits.en: When he tried riding at home, informers called it sedition.
sourceUnits.literal: Later illness gradually improved; at his home mounted horse to test himself; someone reported Han privately practiced riding, suspected as unusual.

sourceUnits.zh: 皝素忌之，遂賜死焉。
sourceUnits.en: Huang, who had always feared him, sent him poison.
sourceUnits.literal: Huang plain envied him; thereupon granted death.

sourceUnits.zh: 翰臨死謂使者曰：「翰懷疑外奔，罪不容誅，不能以骸骨委賊庭，故歸罪有司。
sourceUnits.en: Murong Han told the messenger, “I fled in fear and deserved death, yet I would not die in a foreign hall, so I came home to face judgment.
sourceUnits.literal: Han nearing death told the envoy: “Han harbored suspicion and fled abroad; crime does not permit execution; could not cast bones in the bandit court; therefore returned guilt to the responsible officials.

sourceUnits.zh: 天慈曲湣，不肆之市朝，今日之死，翰之生也。
sourceUnits.en: The king spared me a public execution—this death is mercy.
sourceUnits.literal: Heaven’s kindness bent pity, did not display me in the marketplace; today’s death is Han’s life.

sourceUnits.zh: 但逆胡跨據神州，中原未靖，翰常克心自誓，志吞醜虜，上成先王遺旨，下謝山海之責。
sourceUnits.en: But the rebel Hu barbarians straddle and hold the Divine Land, and the Central Plain is not yet pacified. I always steeled my heart and swore that I would swallow up the vile caitiffs, above to fulfil the late king's dying wish and below to discharge my duty to the realm between the mountains and the sea.
sourceUnits.literal: But the rebellious Hu occupy the Divine Land, and the Central Plain is not yet pacified; Han has always steeled his heart and sworn an oath, intent on swallowing up the vile enemies, above to fulfil the late king's last instructions and below to discharge his duty to the land of mountains and seas.

sourceUnits.zh: 不圖此心不遂，沒有餘恨，命也奈何！」
sourceUnits.en: That hope dies with me—such is fate.”
sourceUnits.literal: Did not expect this heart not to succeed; dying there is surplus regret—fate it—what to do!”

sourceUnits.zh: 仰藥而死。
sourceUnits.en: He drank the poison and died.
sourceUnits.literal: Raised poison and died.

sourceUnits.zh: 陽裕
sourceUnits.en: Yang Yu.
sourceUnits.literal: Yang Yu.

sourceUnits.zh: 陽裕，字士倫，右北平無終人也。
sourceUnits.en: Yang Yu, courtesy name Shilun, came from Wuzhong in right Beiping.
sourceUnits.literal: Yang Yu, courtesy name Shilun, was a man of Wuzhong in Right Beiping.

sourceUnits.zh: 少孤，兄弟皆早亡，單煢獨立，雖宗族無能識者，惟叔父耽幼而奇之，曰：「此兒非惟吾門之標秀，乃佐時之良器也。」
sourceUnits.en: Orphaned young, with brothers dead early, he stood alone; few in the clan knew him, but his uncle Dan marveled at him even in youth and said, "This child is not only our clan's outstanding ornament but an instrument to serve the age."
sourceUnits.literal: In youth orphaned, brothers all died early, alone and solitary; although the lineage group none could recognize him, only uncle Dan in youth wondered at him, saying: “This child is not only our gate’s outstanding show, but an instrument to aid the age.”

sourceUnits.zh: 刺史和演辟為主簿。
sourceUnits.en: Governor He Yan made him chief clerk.
sourceUnits.literal: The governor He Yan summoned him as chief clerk.

sourceUnits.zh: 王浚領州，轉治中從事，忌而不能任。
sourceUnits.en: Under Wang Jun he rose to administration aide but was distrusted.
sourceUnits.literal: Wang Jun held the province, transferred to aide in the bureau of administration, envied yet could not employ him.

sourceUnits.zh: 石勒既克薊城，問棗嵩曰：「幽州人士，誰最可者？」
sourceUnits.en: After Shi Le took Jicheng he asked Zao Song, "Among the gentlemen of Youzhou, who is most worthy?"
sourceUnits.literal: After Shi Le took Ji city, asked Zao Song, saying: “Youzhou gentlemen, who is most worthy?”

sourceUnits.zh: 嵩曰：「燕國劉翰，德素長者。
sourceUnits.en: Zao Song said, "Liu Han of Yan, whose virtue is that of a plain elder.
sourceUnits.literal: Song said: “Yan state’s Liu Han, virtue is plain elder.

sourceUnits.zh: 北平陽裕，幹事之才。」
sourceUnits.en: Yang Yu of Beiping for administrative talent.”
sourceUnits.literal: Beiping’s Yang Yu, talent for handling affairs.”

sourceUnits.zh: 勒曰：「若如君言，王公何以不任？」
sourceUnits.en: Shi Le asked, "If what you say is so, why did Duke Wang not employ him?"
sourceUnits.literal: Le said: “If like your words, why did Duke Wang not employ them?”

sourceUnits.zh: 嵩曰：「王公由不能任，所以為明公擒也。」
sourceUnits.en: Song answered, “Because he could not use them, you captured him.”
sourceUnits.literal: Song said: “Duke Wang because he could not employ them, therefore became the enlightened lord’s captive.”

sourceUnits.zh: 勒方任之，裕乃微服潛遁。
sourceUnits.en: Shi Le meant to employ Yang Yu, who fled in disguise.
sourceUnits.literal: Le was about to employ him; Yu then disguised himself and slipped away.

sourceUnits.zh: 時鮮卑單于段眷為晉驃騎大將軍、遼西公，雅好人物，虛心延裕。
sourceUnits.en: At that time the Xianbei shanyu Duan Juan, who held the Jin titles of General of Agile Cavalry and Duke of Liaoxi, had a refined fondness for men of talent and humbly invited Yang Yu.
sourceUnits.literal: At the time Xianbei Shanyu Duan Juan was Jin’s General of Agile Cavalry and Duke of Liaoxi; by nature he loved men of talent and humbly invited Yu.

sourceUnits.zh: 裕謂友人成泮曰：「仲尼喜佛肸之召，以匏瓜自喻，伊尹亦稱何事非君，何使非民，聖賢尚如此，況吾曹乎！
sourceUnits.en: Yang Yu told his friend Cheng Pan, "Confucius rejoiced at Bi Xi's summons and likened himself to a gourd; Yi Yin too said, 'What affair is not that of the lord? What people are not his subjects?' Even sages were thus, how much more we!
sourceUnits.literal: Yu told friend Cheng Pan, saying: “Confucius rejoiced at Bi Xi’s summons, used the gourd as metaphor; Yi Yin also said what affair is not lord, what people not subjects—even sages were thus; how much more our sort!

sourceUnits.zh: 眷今召我，豈徒然哉！」
sourceUnits.en: Duan Juan’s summons is no empty gesture!”
sourceUnits.literal: Juan now summons me—how could it be vain!”

sourceUnits.zh: 泮曰：「今華夏分崩，九州幅裂，軌跡所及，易水而已。
sourceUnits.en: Cheng Pan replied, “China is shattered; beyond the Yi River there is no refuge.
sourceUnits.literal: Pan said: “Now Huaxia split and crumbling, the nine provinces in tatters, where tracks reach is only to the Yi River.

sourceUnits.zh: 欲偃蹇考槃，以待大通者，俟河之清也。
sourceUnits.en: To hide and wait for peace is to wait for the Yellow River to run clear.
sourceUnits.literal: Desiring to recline and await the great penetration—waiting for the Yellow River to clear—is waiting for the river to clear.

sourceUnits.zh: 人壽幾何？
sourceUnits.en: How long is a life?
sourceUnits.literal: Human life how much?

sourceUnits.zh: 古人以為白駒之歎。
sourceUnits.en: The ancients sighed at time’s white colt.
sourceUnits.literal: The ancients took this as the white colt’s sigh.

sourceUnits.zh: 少遊有雲，郡掾足以廕後，況國相乎！
sourceUnits.en: Shaoyou said that a post as commandery clerk was enough to shelter one's descendants; how much more the post of chancellor of a state!
sourceUnits.literal: Shao You said, a commandery aide suffices to shade posterity—how much more a state chancellor!

sourceUnits.zh: 卿追蹤伊、孔，抑亦知機其神也。」
sourceUnits.en: You follow Confucius and Yi Yin—you know when Heaven calls.”
sourceUnits.literal: You trace Yi and Kong, or also know the moment’s spirit.”

sourceUnits.zh: 裕乃應之。
sourceUnits.en: Yang Yu accepted Duan Juan’s offer.
sourceUnits.literal: Yu thereupon answered him.

sourceUnits.zh: 拜郎中令、中軍將軍，處上卿位。
sourceUnits.en: He was named palace director and central army general, ranking among the highest ministers.
sourceUnits.literal: Appointed Palace Director, Central Army General, occupying the upper minister’s seat.

sourceUnits.zh: 曆事段氏五主，甚見尊重。
sourceUnits.en: He served five successive Duan lords and won deep respect.
sourceUnits.literal: Passed through serving the Duan house’s five lords, greatly was respected.

sourceUnits.zh: 段遼與皝相攻，裕諫曰：「臣聞親仁善鄰，國之寶也。
sourceUnits.en: When Duan Liao and Murong Huang clashed, Yang Yu urged, “A state’s greatest treasure is to cherish kindness and befriend one’s neighbors.
sourceUnits.literal: Duan Liao and Huang attacked each other; Yu remonstrated, saying: “I have heard that cherishing benevolence and befriending neighbors is the state’s treasure.

sourceUnits.zh: 慕容與國世為婚姻，且皝令德之主，不宜連兵構怨，凋殘百姓。
sourceUnits.en: The Murong house and yours have intermarried for generations; Murong Huang is a man of virtue—you must not exhaust the people in vendetta.
sourceUnits.literal: Murong and the state generation after generation are marriage; moreover Huang is a lord of ordered virtue; ought not join arms and build resentment, withering the common people.

sourceUnits.zh: 臣恐禍害之興，將由於此。
sourceUnits.en: I fear calamity will come of this feud.
sourceUnits.literal: Your servant fears the rise of disaster and harm will stem from this.

sourceUnits.zh: 願兩追前失，通款如初，使國家有太山之安，蒼生蒙息肩之惠。」
sourceUnits.en: Let both sides forget old quarrels and restore peace so the realm stands firm as Taishan and the people can lay down their burdens.”
sourceUnits.literal: Wish both pursue former faults, communicate sincerity as at the beginning, cause the state to have Mount Tai’s peace, the black-haired people to receive the favor of resting shoulders.”

sourceUnits.zh: 遼不從。
sourceUnits.en: Duan Liao refused.
sourceUnits.literal: Liao did not follow.

sourceUnits.zh: 出為燕郡太守。
sourceUnits.en: He left court to become grand warden of Yan commandery.
sourceUnits.literal: Went out as Yan commandery grand warden.

sourceUnits.zh: 石季龍克令支，裕以郡降，拜北平太守，徵為尚書左丞。
sourceUnits.en: When Shi Hu seized Lingzhi, Yang Yu surrendered his commandery, was named grand warden of Beiping, then recalled as left assistant in the secretariat.
sourceUnits.literal: Shi Jilong took Lingzhi; Yu with the commandery surrendered; appointed Beiping grand warden; summoned as Left Assistant to the Masters of Writing.

sourceUnits.zh: 段遼之請迎于季龍也，裕以左丞領征東麻秋司馬。
sourceUnits.en: When Duan Liao asked Shi Hu to send troops to receive him, Yang Yu, while serving as Left Assistant, concurrently served as marshal to Ma Qiu, General Who Campaigns in the East.
sourceUnits.literal: When Duan Liao requested that Jilong receive him, Yu, as Left Assistant, concurrently served as marshal to Ma Qiu, General Who Campaigns in the East.

sourceUnits.zh: 秋敗，裕為軍人所執，將詣皝。
sourceUnits.en: Ma Qiu’s defeat left Yang Yu a prisoner on his way to Murong Huang.
sourceUnits.literal: When Qiu was defeated, Yu was seized by soldiers, was about to be brought to Huang.

sourceUnits.zh: 皝素聞裕名，即命釋其囚，拜郎中令，遷大將軍左司馬。
sourceUnits.en: Murong Huang, who had long admired him, freed him at once, named him palace director, then promoted him to senior major on his staff.
sourceUnits.literal: Huang plain had heard Yu’s name; immediately ordered release his bonds; appointed Palace Director; promoted Grand General’s Left Major.

sourceUnits.zh: 東破高句麗，北滅宇文歸，皆豫其謀，皝甚器重之。
sourceUnits.en: He helped plan the eastern victory over Goguryeo and the northern destruction of Yuwen Gui, and Huang came to rely on him heavily.
sourceUnits.literal: East defeated Goguryeo, north destroyed Yuwen Gui—both he pre-planned their strategies; Huang greatly prized and employed him.

sourceUnits.zh: 及遷都和龍，裕雅有巧思，皝所制城池宮闔，皆裕之規模。
sourceUnits.en: When the capital shifted to Helong, Yang Yu’s engineering shaped every wall and tower Murong Huang built.
sourceUnits.literal: When moved the capital to Helong, Yu by nature had clever thought; the city walls and palace towers Huang regulated were all Yu’s models.

sourceUnits.zh: 裕雖仕皝日近，寵秩在舊人之右，性謙恭清儉，剛簡慈篤，雖曆居朝端，若布衣之士。
sourceUnits.en: Though he rose above older favorites, he lived modestly and treated everyone like a poor scholar.
sourceUnits.literal: Although Yu served Huang daily nearer, favor and rank above the old men’s, nature humble and respectful, clear and frugal, firm, simple, kind, and earnest; although passed through dwelling at court’s apex, like a scholar in plain cloth.

sourceUnits.zh: 士大夫流亡羈絕者，莫不經營收葬，存恤孤遺，士無賢不肖皆傾身待之，是以所在推仰。
sourceUnits.en: He buried exiles, aided their orphans, and honored every gentleman he met, winning universal esteem.
sourceUnits.literal: Grandees and scholars who fled in exile and were cut off—none he did not arrange burial for, preserve and pity orphans left behind; gentry whether worthy or not all he inclined his person to treat; therefore wherever he was was pushed and looked up to.

sourceUnits.zh: 初，范陽盧諶每稱之曰：「吾及晉之清平，曆觀朝士多矣，忠清簡毅，篤信義烈，如陽士倫者，實亦未幾。」
sourceUnits.en: Lu Chen of Fanyang once said, “In times of peace I have known many officials, but few match Yang Yu in loyalty, austerity, and steadfast faith.”
sourceUnits.literal: In the beginning, Fan Yang’s Lu Chen always praised him, saying: “I have reached Jin’s clear peace, broadly viewed many court gentlemen; loyal, pure, concise, resolute, faithful in duty and fierce in righteousness—like Yang Shilun, in truth also not many.”

sourceUnits.zh: 及死，皝甚悼之，時年六十二。
sourceUnits.en: When he died at sixty-two, Murong Huang mourned him deeply.
sourceUnits.literal: When he died, Huang greatly mourned him; at the time age sixty-two sui.
